LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.

2.– ACTIVITY 9: PREPOSITIONS, TR#9 (4’)
> Warm-Up
The Ss should perform the following actions to rehearse 
the movements.
•	 March in line. (all the Ss march in a single file line)
•	 Hide under the table.
•	 Walk next to a friend.
•	 Stand between two chairs.
•	 Jump behind the teacher. (all the Ss jump on the spot 
behind the teacher)
•	 Run in front of the (white) board. (all the Ss run on 
the spot in front of the board)
•	 Sit on a chair.
> Main Activity
Then play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance 
to it.
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.

Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.
3.– STORY (PP.8-16) (8’)
Tell the Ss the second half of the story using the Big Book. 
Please see the section on S storytelling in the Warm-Up routines 
index. Before telling the second half of the story, it is advisable 
to ask some recap questions such as:
•	 “Who do Pam and Paul live with?” 
“Pam and Paul live with their family.”
•	 “When is Pam and Paul’s birthday?” 
“Pam and Paul’s birthday is on Sunday.”
•	 “What do Pam and Paul want for their birthday?” 
“Pam and Paul want to adopt a puppy.”
•	 “What is the puppy’s name?” 
“His name is Billy.”

NOTE: if you collected your Ss’ books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying, “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
In this activity, Ss must answer story comprehension questions 
and place the stickers depicting story events on the correct 
day. This serves as a review of what Pam and Paul must do 
in the story.
Give out the stickers and the student book and model the 
task. Pointing to Monday, ask a S, “What must Pam and Paul 
do on Monday?”. They should answer, “On Monday, Pam and 
Paul must wash Billy.” Then all the Ss find the correct sticker 
and stick it on the “Monday” calendar. To continue with the 
rest of the week, Ss should take it in turns to ask questions 
about the story to other Ss. Then, all the Ss place the correct 
sticker where it belongs.
> Phrases for the worksheet:
What must Pam and Paul do on... (day of the week)? 
•	 On Monday, Pam and Paul must wash Billy. 
•	 On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy. 
•	 On Wednesday, Pam and Paul must take Billy for a walk. 
•	 On Thursday, Pam and Paul must pick up Billy’s poo. 
•	 On Friday, Pam and Paul must give Billy some water. 
•	 On Saturday, Pam and Paul must brush Billy. 
What happens on Sunday? 
•	 On Sunday, Billy is with Grandma, and Pam and Paul 
must take better care of Billy! 
If time allows, review the content by saying incorrect statements 
and having the Ss correct you. Say, for example, “On Monday 
Pam and Paul must brush Billy” to which they should answer, 
“No, that’s wrong! On Monday Pam and Paul must wash Billy.”

6.– ACTIVITY 5: DAYS OF THE WEEK CARD GAME (8’)

> How to Play
This is based on the traditional card game Go Fish. The point 
of the game is to find pairs of matching cards by asking the 
other players for them. In this case, Ss must match the day of 
the week and the chore that Pam and Paul had to do that day.
> Warm-Up
Bring a SB with you and use p.4 (Story Comprehension) 
as a visual aid. Preferably, the worksheet would have been 
completed previously.
Show the Monday card (P.1.5) and ask the Ss “What must 
Pam and Paul do on Monday?”. Ss must answer, “On Monday, 
Pam and Paul must wash Billy.”. Review the whole week in 
the same manner:
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Monday?” 	
 
“On Monday, Pam and Paul must wash Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Tuesday?” 	
 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Wednesday?” 	 
“On Wednesday, Pam and Paul must take Billy for 
a walk.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Thursday?” 	  
“On Thursday, Pam and Paul must pick up Billy’s poo.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Friday?” 	
 
“On Friday, Pam and Paul must give Billy some water.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Saturday?” 	  
“On Saturday, Pam and Paul must brush Billy.” 
•	 “What happens on Sunday?” 	
 
“On Sunday, Billy is with Grandma.” 
> Main Activity
To play, you should first shuffle the cards (P.1.5) while saying, 
“Mix, mix, mix” and have the Ss say, “Stop!”.

Then deal three cards to each S and put the rest of the cards 
in a pile face down on the table. Explain to the Ss that they 
must find pairs. Ss must ask another S for a card and try to 
match it with one of the cards in their hand. They can either 
ask for the day of the week or the chore: 
•	 “Jane, have you got Friday?”
•	 “Jane, have you got ‘brush Billy’?”
Jane should either:
•	 Say “Yes, I have, here you are!” and hand it over to 
the S who asked for it. 
•	 Say “No, I haven’t. Take a card!” and the S who asked 
must pick up a card from the deck. 
When a S finds a pair, they must then place the pair face 
up on the table and say, “I’ve got a pair!”. After that, it is the 
next Ss’ turn. 
The game continues with the Ss taking turns asking for the 
card they need from the other players. If a player gets all their 
cards stolen, they have to draw a card from the pile on their turn. 
The game is over when there are no cards left on the deck in 
the middle, or when time is up. At this point, ask the Ss one by 
one, “How many pairs have you got?” and the S must answer, 
“I’ve got five pairs.” The S with the most pairs is the winner.
NOTE: if you have a small group, you might want to halve 
the deck to speed up the activity. 
> Follow-Up
Take the winner’s pairs and ask the group: “What pairs has 
Jane got?”. Point to the cards and elicit from the whole group: 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy. On Monday...” 
7.– ACTIVITY 1: MY CHORES (9’)
P.1.1
P.1.1
P.1.1

TARGET LANGUAGE FOR FUN ACTIVITIES
Play video games
Read a book
Listen to music
Talk on the phone
Watch TV
Draw a picture
Ride my bike
Play football
Roller-skate
Play in the park
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR CHORES
Wash Billy
Feed Billy
Take Billy for a walk
Brush Billy
Give Billy some water
Pick up Billy’s poo
Lay the table
Make the bed
Take out the rubbish
Sweep the floor
Clear the table 
> How to Play
Ss must find the activities that match those on their bingo 
board. In order to win, the Ss must find all their chores first, 
and then their fun activity.
> Warm-Up
Start by drilling the target language. Spread the Chores cards 
(P.1.1) on the table and say: “Wow! Look at my chores. I have 
a lot of things to do! I have to feed Billy (signal to the Ss to 
repeat after you), wash Billy, etc.” 
Now review the fun activities. Start by saying: “This is what I 
want to do. I want to...”. Show the Ss the fun activity cards one 
by one and let them finish the sentence with the fun activity. 
> Main Activity
Hand out an A5 Bingo Board (P.1.1) to each S. Then spread 
out the Memory cards, which show the chores and fun activities 
(P.1.1), face down on the table.
Choose a S to go first. You can check out the different tips on 
how to start a game at the beginning of this guide. The S turns 
over a Memory card and identifies the activity by saying one of 
the following phrases depending on the scenario:
•	 If they have it: “I have to...”
•	 If they don’t have it: “I don’t have to...”
•	 If they find a fun activity before their chores: “I can’t ... 
now, I must ... first.” For instance: “I can’t play video 
games now, I must wash the puppy, clear the table 
and make the bed first.”

The first S to collect all their chores followed by their fun 
activity is the winner.
> Follow-Up
Once you have finished the activity, point to the winner’s 
board and ask the Ss, “What chores must Jane do first?” to 
which they should reply “Jane must clear the table, take out 
the rubbish and make the bed first and then she can listen 
to music.”.
8.– ACTIVITY 7: SWITCH! (5’)
> How to Play
This is a group hand clapping game to practise counting. To 
play, you must have all the Ss sitting in a circle, either on the 
floor or at the table.
> Main Activity
If you do the activity sitting on chairs, the Ss should sit with 
their palms facing up on the table. If you do it on the floor, the 
Ss place their palms on their legs.
The Ss must place their right hand on top of the hand of the 
S sitting to their right, and their left hand underneath the hand 
of the person on their left. This way when they begin to clap, 
they will use their right hand to clap the hand of the person 
to their left and the clapping will continue around the circle.
Start counting from number 50 until you get to 99. If someone 
makes a mistake, the Ss switch the position of their hands (right 
hand below, left hand on top). If this is too difficult, simply move 
on with the game without switching hand positions.
NOTE: if time allows, increase the difficulty by starting from 
number one or counting backwards.

ACTIVITY 4: CHARADES (VERSION 2)
P.1.2
Play the game in the Pictionary style, using the whiteboard. 
A S must take a Fun Activity card (P.1.2), ask the group “What 
am I doing?”, and draw the action on the board. The rest of the 
Ss try to guess by asking, “Are you watching TV?” to which the 
S must reply, “Yes, I am.” or “No, I’m not.”. To ensure everyone 
gets a turn, set a timer for each round (30 seconds should be 
enough).
